question_text: The C–C bond length in graphite is shorter than the C–C bond length in diamond. Explain.

steps.why: The question states a fact and asks for the reason, so the two measured values are written down first. They also fix which bond in graphite is meant: the 141.5 pm is the distance between carbon atoms inside a sheet, not the distance between the sheets.
common_mistakes: Quoting one bond length for carbon. The C–C distance is 141.5 pm in graphite and 154 pm in diamond.
Comparing the graphite value with the distance between graphite's sheets. The 141.5 pm is the C–C distance inside a sheet.
steps.memory_tip: Graphite is the shorter one: 141.5 pm against 154 pm.
steps.margin_note: Write both numbers with the substance named beside each.

steps.label: Why the graphite bond is shorter
lines: In diamond each carbon is sp³ and every
C–C bond is a plain single sigma bond.
In graphite each carbon is sp², and its
fourth electron is delocalised over the
sheet, so every C–C bond inside a sheet
A bond with double bond character is
shorter and stronger than a single bond.
An sp² orbital also has more s character
than an sp³ orbital, and greater s

lines.text: Double bond character shortens the bond

steps.why: Two effects push in the same direction. The delocalised electrons add some double bond character to every C–C bond in a sheet, and an sp² orbital holds its electrons closer to the nucleus than an sp³ orbital does, so both make the graphite bond shorter than the plain single bond in diamond.
common_mistakes: Saying the graphite bond is shorter because graphite is softer. Softness comes from the weak forces between the sheets, and has nothing to do with the bond length inside a sheet.
Writing that graphite has full double bonds. Each C–C bond in a sheet has partial double bond character, because the fourth electron is delocalised over the whole sheet.
steps.memory_tip: Partial double bond character means a shorter bond.
steps.margin_note: The delocalised fourth electron is the reason; write it in words, not only as sp² against sp³.

insider_note: A complete answer gives both numbers, 141.5 pm for graphite and 154 pm for diamond, and then the reason: the delocalised fourth electron gives every bond inside a graphite sheet partial double bond character.
